namiStop.name: Nami Island (Namiseom)
namiStop.description:
Nami Island opens the day's second chapter with a 5-minute ferry crossing from Gapyeong Wharf onto a half-moon-shaped river island in the Bukhan River. Approximately **460,000 m² (140,000 pyeong) and ~5 km in circumference**, Namiseom is named after **General Nami (Nam Yi, 1441-1468)**, a Joseon-era military commander executed at age 28 after being falsely accused of treason during the reign of King Yejong. 

The island originally became land only during floods; **in 1944 the Japanese colonial government built the Cheongpyeong Dam, raising the river level and making Nami a permanent island**. It found global fame **in 2002 as the filming location for KBS drama 'Winter Sonata'** starring Bae Yong-joon and Choi Ji-woo — the catalyst for the early 2000s Hallyu wave — and continues to draw about **3.3 million visitors annually (1.3 million foreign)**, making it Korea's most-visited single tourist destination after Seoul, Busan, and Jeju. 

Since **March 1, 2006** the island has branded itself as the self-declared **'Naminara Republic'** with its own flag, currency (Nami Tongbo coins), passport, and postal service — a tourism marketing concept rather than an actual political entity. 

The signature **Metasequoia tree-lined avenue** (Winter Sonata's iconic snowy lane), the **Riverside Lover's Ginkgo Tree Lane** on the south side, the **Korean Pine Road**, and the recycled-glass **Sequoia Bridge** made from soju bottles are all walkable in a relaxed two hours. On-island wildlife includes peacocks (including rare albinos), ostriches, wild rabbits, and squirrels. 

**The Naminara Republic VISA Fee (round-trip ferry included) is included in this tour price**.

Iconic Metasequoia tree-lined avenue — Winter Sonata (2002) signature filming location

**UNICEF Child Friendly Park designation 2010** + Nami Island Arts & Education hosts **600+ performances/exhibitions/festivals annually**
timeUsed: Ferry crossing from Gapyeong Wharf (5-10 minutes including queue)
Free walking time along the Metasequoia / Ginkgo / Korean Pine avenues — half-island circuit ~3 km
Optional bicycle rental (single 7,000 / tandem 14,000 KRW per hour) or electric blue train (3,000 KRW one-way to UNICEF Hall)

namiStop.whyOnRoute: Nami Island comes second after Seoraksan because the **Seoraksan → Nami drive (~2 hours via Inje-Hongcheon-Chuncheon)** lands the coach at Gapyeong Wharf around 14:30 — past the heaviest 11:00-14:00 ferry-line peak and with afternoon side-light still available for the Metasequoia avenue photography. The 2-hour stop allows a comfortable ferry round-trip plus the half-island circuit covering the three tree-lined avenues without rushing. Pairing Nami with Morning Calm in the same afternoon also leverages the **30-minute drive** between them — both are in the Gapyeong/Cheongpyeong corridor that the day's east-west axis already traverses.

smartNotes.photo: Metasequoia avenue is the world-famous Winter Sonata shot — best in autumn (golden, late October-early November) or winter (snow). Riverside Lover's Ginkgo Tree Lane on the south side is quieter and equally photogenic. Albino peacock occasionally appears near Lover's Lane.
smartNotes.facilities: On-island restaurants serve Korean comfort food (hotteok, sweet potato latte, tteok-galbi). Sonata Cafe in a traditional hanok is the signature stop. Foreign-card-friendly ticket counter at Gapyeong Wharf — ticket machines do not accept foreign cards, ask at the counter.

gmcStop.name: The Garden of Morning Calm
gmcStop.description:
About 30 minutes south of Nami Island, the Garden of Morning Calm is **Korea's signature private arboretum** — approximately **330,000 m²** of curated landscape with around **5,000 plant species**. Conceived in **1992** and opened to the public in **1996**, the garden was designed and personally cultivated by **Han Sang-kyung of Sahmyook University**, who at one point sold his house to fund the project; the name draws from Korea's longstanding nickname '**Land of the Morning Calm**' (Joseon). 

**Twenty themed sub-gardens** — including the **Sunken Garden shaped like the Korean peninsula**, the Hometown House Garden, the Bonsai Garden, the Moonlight Garden, the Sky Path, and the Garden of Eden — each carry their own visual identity and have served as filming sets for many K-dramas including **Moonlight Drawn by Clouds**. 

From early December to mid-March every winter, the garden hosts **Korea's first natural-environment lighting festival** with more than **200,000 environmentally-friendly LED bulbs** covering the grounds, transforming the garden after sunset into a winter wonderland. 

**The name 'Garden of Morning Calm'** comes from Indian poet Rabindranath Tagore, who in 1929 referred to Korea as 'the Land of Morning Calm.' Han Sang-kyung conceived the project in 1992 while serving as exchange professor in the United States, where he was inspired by world-class private gardens. 

**Han and his wife designed and personally labored on the garden**, and during periods of financial difficulty they sold their family home and lived in a small dwelling on the garden's property to continue construction. 

The garden first opened to the public on May 11, 1996, with 10 themed sections; today it has expanded to 20 themed sub-gardens across 330,000 m². **Admission is INCLUDED in this tour price**.
highlights: Korea's signature private arboretum — 330,000 m² with ~5,000 plant species
Founded by Han Sang-kyung of Sahmyook University; opened 1996 (conceived 1992)
Winter Lighting Festival December - March with 200,000+ LEDs (Korea's first natural-environment light festival)
20 themed sub-gardens — Sunken Garden shaped like the Korean peninsula, Moonlight Garden, Bonsai Garden, Garden of Eden
K-drama filming location for Moonlight Drawn by Clouds and others

**Conceived 1992 / land purchased 1994 / opened May 11, 1996**: Founder Prof. Han Sang-kyung and his wife designed and personally cultivated the entire garden, even selling their house during early financial hardship

**Selected by CNN as one of Korea's Top 50 Tourist Attractions** — the Sunken Garden's Korean Peninsula shape (10 large/small flower beds expressing yearning for unification) is the CNN-cited landmark feature
**Cheonnyeonhyang (Chinese juniper)** is the official symbol of Morning Calm — the garden's signature plant species among the 5,000 total catalogued
timeUsed: Garden entry and brief orientation by the driver-guide (~5 min)
Free walking time across the 20 themed sub-gardens (~50 min)
Optional Sunken Garden (Korean Peninsula shape) extended photo time (~10 min)
Winter visits: arrival timed for 17:00 illumination start to see daytime garden + lighting festival ignition
gmcStop.whyOnRoute: Morning Calm closes the day with its calmest visual chapter, ~30 minutes south of Nami Island. The 17:00 arrival aligns perfectly with the **Winter Lighting Festival illumination ignition (December 5 - March 15)** — guests effectively pay one entry fee but experience two distinct visual gardens (daytime arboretum + night LED festival). In non-festival months, the same 17:00 window captures the **transitional afternoon light** that the garden's photography reputation depends on. The 70-minute stop is intentionally compact — enough for the Sunken Garden, Moonlight Garden, and one or two other themed sub-gardens — and respects the day's 19:00 Seoul-return target.

smartNotes.photo: Spring (cherry blossoms April), summer (lush greens), autumn (foliage October-early November), and winter (lighting festival post-sunset) all photograph differently. The light tunnels at dusk during festival period are the iconic shot.
smartNotes.facilities: Food Garden serves Korean comfort food (soybean-paste stew, vegetable bibimbap, snow cheese tteokbokki). Good Morning Coffee in a hanok roasting house is the signature cafe. Restaurants close at 20:00.
smartNotes.tip: For the lighting festival (Dec 5 - Mar 15), the 17:00 arrival catches both daytime garden colours and the illumination ignition. Heavy snow February gives the most magical Frozen-movie scene.

petiteStop.name: Petite France
petiteStop.description:
The day's compact final stop, Petite France is a French cultural theme village built into a hillside above Cheongpyeong Lake about 25 minutes from Nami Island. Opened in July 2008 by founder Han Hong-seop, the 16-building village is themed around 'flowers, stars, and the Little Prince' (Antoine de Saint-Exupéry's 1943 novel Le Petit Prince) and houses a Saint-Exupéry memorial hall, the Orgel House (a collection of antique music boxes featuring a 200-year-old centerpiece that still plays), a French housing exhibition, a marionette theater, and a gallery of le coq gaulois (Gallic rooster) sculptures and paintings. 

Drama fans visit primarily for the K-drama legacy: Petite France was the filming location for Beethoven Virus (2008), Personal Taste (2010), Secret Garden (2010), My Love from the Star (2013-2014), the 2025 hit Bon Appétit Your Majesty (Maison de Marie doubled as Im Yoon-ah's character's room), and the popular variety show Running Man. 

The adjacent Pinocchio & Da Vinci Italian Village offers a combo ticket option for visitors with extra time. The site has been selected for the 2026 Korea-France 140th Anniversary Commemorative Program. 

The village serves a dual function: French cultural theme village + the **Goseong Youth Training Center** that accommodates up to 200 visitors in 4-to-10-person rooms for educational stays. 

The site's most distinctive architectural feature is the **Traditional France Residence Gallery**: an entire 19th-century French farmhouse from middle-region France, dismantled and reassembled on-site using 200+-year-old wood, roof tiles, and bricks — joined entirely without nails using traditional French timber-frame mortise-and-tenon technique. 

Petite France is also **Korea's only Saint-Exupéry Foundation-licensed organization**, meaning every Little Prince motif on-site is officially authorized by the Foundation in France. 

The adjacent Pinocchio & Da Vinci Italian Village (separate ticket or combo at ₩19,500 adult) extends the day's European-village content by ~45 min if desired.

K-drama filming credits: Beethoven Virus (2008), Personal Taste (2010), Secret Garden (2010), My Love from the Star (2013-14), Bon Appétit Your Majesty (2025)
Orgel House: 200-year-old music box collection; Marionette theater with daily performances
Adjacent Pinocchio & Da Vinci Italian Village — combo tickets 19,500 KRW adult
Selected for the 2026 Korea-France 140th Anniversary Commemorative Program

**2025 K-drama 'Bon Appétit, Your Majesty' filming location**: 'Maison de Marie' doubles as Yeon Ji-yeong's (IM YOON-AH) contemporary-Korea apartment — adds to existing K-drama portfolio (Beethoven Virus 2008, Personal Taste 2010, Secret Garden 2010, My Love from the Star 2013, Vincenzo 2021)

**Daily admission 2026**: ₩10,000 adult / ₩8,000 teen / ₩6,000 child; Combo with adjacent Pinocchio & Da Vinci Italian Village ₩19,500 adult; Sun-Thu 09:00-18:00, Fri-Sat 09:00-20:00 (last admission 1 hour before closing)

petiteStop.whyOnRoute: Placed last, Petite France gives the day a lighter, photo-friendly close after the broader walks at Nami Island and the visual richness of Morning Calm. Its compact scale (1.5-2 hours typical) fits naturally into the late-afternoon energy window — visitors who arrive after 16:00 also get the daytime + early-evening illumination contrast on the village's pastel facades. For atockorea's overseas-Chinese-diaspora and SE-Asia segments, **Petite France's K-drama density** (Beethoven Virus 2008, Personal Taste 2010, Secret Garden 2010, My Love from the Star 2013, Vincenzo 2021, 2025's Bon Appétit Your Majesty with IM YOON-AH) is the day's strongest Hallyu touchpoint — Maison de Marie alone has appeared in 6+ K-dramas making it one of the most-photographed building exteriors in the broader Gapyeong tourism zone. Combined with the licensed Saint-Exupéry Foundation status, the village delivers an authenticated Western-cultural-anchor stop that contrasts well with Nami Island's Korean-peninsula pastoralism and Morning Calm's Korean-garden classicism, giving the day three distinct visual vocabularies.

visitBasics.admission: Adult 12,000 KRW / Teen 8,500 / Child 7,500 KRW (combined Petite France + Italian Village 19,500 KRW adult)
visitBasics.walking: Easy — small flat-to-gentle-slope village (1-1.5 hours to explore)

smartNotes.photo: Pastel-colored timber-framed houses against the green mountain backdrop are the signature shots. The viewing deck at the top of the hill offers the best wide composition. K-drama scene-spotting is a guided activity for fans (Saint-Exupéry building = My Love from the Star pivotal scenes).
smartNotes.facilities: Snack stalls only — waffles, dumplings, fish-cake soup, coffee. Most visitors eat at adjacent Italian Village or in nearby Cheongpyeong town instead.
smartNotes.tip: Best paired with Nami Island and/or Garden of Morning Calm via the Gapyeong City Tour Bus for self-guided trips. Late-afternoon arrival lets you see daytime + early-evening illumination. Visitors expecting a large attraction often note the modest scale (1.5-2 hours typical) — manage expectations.

practicalItems.title: Pickup & drop-off
practicalItems.preview: Two Seoul pickup points: Starbucks Hongik University Station Exit 8 at 06:00…
content: Two Seoul pickup points: **Starbucks Hongik University Station Exit 8 at 06:00** (Mapo-gu), and **Myeongdong Station Exit 2 (NorthFace flagship) at 06:30** (Jung-gu).
Both pickups share the same coach; please be at your chosen point 5 minutes early.
Return drop-offs in reverse order: **Myeongdong ~19:00, Hongik ~19:30**.
Friday/Sunday evenings may run 30 min later due to expressway traffic — notify the guide if you have a hard schedule.

practicalItems.title: What to wear & bring
practicalItems.preview: Comfortable closed-toe walking shoes for Seoraksan paths (rocky in places)…
content: Comfortable closed-toe walking shoes for Seoraksan paths (rocky in places).
Warm layers October-March; Seoraksan altitude is 5-7°C colder than Seoul.
Camera or smartphone (Nami Metasequoia avenue and Morning Calm are the photo highlights).
Cash and card for lunch (~₩10,000-15,000) and optional Seorak Cable Car (₩16,000) if you plan to ride.
Light snacks if you start without breakfast — first food stop is around 13:00-13:30 en route to Nami.

practicalItems.title: Weather policy
content: Year-round operation.
Light rain: tour runs as scheduled — Nami and Morning Calm both have charm in rain; Seoraksan's lower paths remain walkable with grip shoes.
Heavy rain: Seorak Cable Car typically suspended in storm conditions (refunded if pre-paid); the guide will steer guests to the Biseondae walk or extended Sinheungsa visit instead.
Typhoon-level weather or expressway closure: full refund or rebooking offered.

practicalItems.title: What's included
practicalItems.preview: Two Seoul pickups, large coach, English-speaking guide, Nami and Morning Calm admissions…
content: Two Seoul pickup points and same drop-off points, air-conditioned large coach, licensed English-speaking guide.
**Nami Island ferry round-trip + Naminara Republic VISA Fee (₩19,000) — INCLUDED**.
**The Garden of Morning Calm admission (₩11,000) — INCLUDED**.
**Seoraksan National Park entrance — FREE (abolished May 2023)**.
**NOT included**: lunch en route (~₩10,000-15,000), optional Seorak Cable Car (₩16,000 round-trip, on-site ticketing only).

practicalItems.title: Language
content: Primary tour language: English.
Chinese-speaking guide available on request — book 3+ days ahead.
Korean spoken throughout the day for menus, signage, and stall interactions; the guide handles translation.

practicalItems.title: Walking & terrain
content: Moderate.
Seoraksan: easy at Sinheungsa Temple base; moderate on the Biseondae walk; challenging if you choose Heundeulbawi or Ulsanbawi (stairs).
Nami Island: flat, paved tree-lined avenues; ~3 km in 2 hours is the typical pace.
Morning Calm: rolling terrain, mostly paved garden paths.
Total walking ≈4-5 km plus the optional Seoraksan stairs.
Strollers viable at Nami and partially at Morning Calm; not at Seoraksan upper trails.

practicalItems.title: Lunch (own expense)
practicalItems.preview: Lunch is taken en route from Seoraksan to Nami, around 13:30…
content: Lunch is taken en route from Seoraksan to Nami, around 13:30 at a local restaurant in the Inje-Chuncheon corridor.
Typical choices: Chuncheon dakgalbi (the region's most-famous dish — sweet-spicy stir-fried chicken with cabbage and rice cakes), kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup), or bibimbap (~₩10,000-15,000).
Vegetarian and halal-friendly options possible with advance notice — please notify at booking.

practicalItems.title: Cancellation
practicalItems.preview: Free cancellation up to 24 hours before pickup.
content: Free cancellation up to 24 hours before pickup.
Inside 24 hours: 50% refund.
No-show or missed pickup: no refund — but contact AtoC Korea operations within 10 minutes of pickup time and the coach may briefly wait if running ahead of schedule.

practicalWeatherStatic._seasonalSummary: Seoul + Gangwon: temperate four-season climate. Seoraksan is 5-7°C cooler than Seoul year-round. Hot humid summers (Jun-Aug), crisp cold winters (Dec-Feb), with prime seasons in spring (April cherry blossoms) and autumn (October-November foliage).

bookingTrustItems.title: All admissions included
bookingTrustItems.body: Nami Island ferry (₩19,000) and Garden of Morning Calm (₩11,000) admissions are pre-paid into the tour price — no per-stop ticket queues. Seoraksan entrance is FREE (abolished May 2023). Total admission savings: ~₩30,000.

bookingTrustItems.title: Licensed English-speaking guide
bookingTrustItems.body: Korea Tourism Organization-licensed guide with English fluency; Chinese-speaking guide available on advance request. Guide narration covers Seoraksan's Silla-era temple history, Nami's Winter Sonata legacy, and Morning Calm's founder story.

bookingTrustItems.title: Transparent pricing
bookingTrustItems.body: No ginseng shops, no duty-free, no commissioned souvenir detours. Every minute of the 13-hour day is at an attraction or in transit — what you book is what you experience.
